subject: physics_2
question_text: Why is the electric field always at right angles to the equipotential surface? Explain.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: the book argues from dV = E dr cos θ = 0 with E, dr non-zero, giving cos θ = 0, θ = 90° — correct; written here through the work W = qΔV = 0 on the surface, the same chain with the physical meaning attached.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The zero-work argument
lines: Moving a test charge q through dr anywhere
on an equipotential surface needs no work,
because V does not change there:

lines.text: dW = qE dr cos θ = q dV = 0

lines: E and dr are not zero, so cos θ = 0.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the work equation and force cos θ to zero.
steps.why: The only factor in qE dr cos θ that can be zero is cos θ, because the field exists and the movement is real. That one factor carries the whole conclusion.
common_mistakes: Setting E = 0 instead of cos θ = 0. The field is not zero on the surface.
Forgetting to say dV = 0 on the surface — that is what makes the work zero.

recall.must_convey: That no work is done moving a charge on the surface, so qE dr cos θ = 0, and only cos θ can be zero.
accept: no work on an equipotential surface
E dr cos theta is zero

steps.memory_tip: Zero work, non-zero E, non-zero dr — the zero must sit in cos θ.

steps.label: The conclusion
lines: cos θ = 0 gives θ = 90°. The field E makes a
right angle with every line drawn on the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State θ = 90° and say it in words: E is perpendicular to the surface.
steps.why: If E had any component along the surface, that component would do work on a charge moved along it and V would change — against the definition of the surface. So the whole of E must point across it.
common_mistakes: Boxing cos θ = 0 and stopping. The asked conclusion is θ = 90°.

recall.must_convey: That θ is 90 degrees, so E is perpendicular to the equipotential surface.
accept: E is perpendicular to the surface
at right angles to the surface

steps.memory_tip: Any part of E along the surface would do work there — so no part of E lies along it.

insider_note: The chain dV = 0 → cos θ = 0 → θ = 90° must all appear; jumping straight to perpendicular loses the working mark.
